confirm.title: Add this Enigma2 receiver
confirm.description:
Enigma2 box {name} ({boxtype}, {image}) has announced itself on the broker.

Adding it switches the box into integration mode: the plugin withdraws the MQTT discovery entities it publishes on its own, and Home Assistant builds the device instead. The box has to confirm the switch before it is added.

user.title: Add an Enigma2 receiver by hand
user.description: Use this when the receiver's announcement never reached Home Assistant, for example because the box publishes through an MQTT bridge that rewrites the topic prefix.

data_description.base_topic: The prefix the receiver publishes under, as Home Assistant sees it on the broker. The plugin's default is `enigma2`.
data_description.node_id: The receiver's node ID, shown on the plugin's setup screen. It is the box type and the last six digits of the MAC address, for example `vuuno4kse_005301`.
data_description.name: What to call this receiver in Home Assistant. Left empty, the name the plugin reports is used.

reconfigure.title: Change where this receiver publishes
reconfigure.description:
Use this after changing the node ID or the base topic on the receiver's own setup screen.

Changing the node ID changes the receiver's identity: its entities are rebuilt with new IDs and their history stays with the old device, which is removed. Changing only the base topic or the name keeps everything.

data_description.base_topic: The prefix the receiver publishes under, as Home Assistant sees it on the broker.
data_description.node_id: The receiver's node ID, shown on the plugin's setup screen.
data_description.name: What to call this receiver in Home Assistant.

error.no_ack: The receiver did not confirm the mode switch. Check that the plugin is running and that its broker login may write to this node's topics.
error.not_found: No receiver was found on this topic. Check the base topic and the node ID on the plugin's setup screen.
error.invalid_topic: That is not a usable topic. The base topic and the node ID must not contain the `+` or `#` wildcards.
error.already_configured: Another receiver is already configured with that node ID.

abort.already_in_progress: This receiver is already being added.
abort.mqtt_unavailable: The MQTT integration is not available. Set it up first, then add the receiver.
abort.not_enigma2_announcement: That message is not an Enigma2 MQTT Bridge announcement.
abort.retracted: The receiver has withdrawn its announcement.

init.title: Receiver options
init.description: The receiver reports the MAC address {mac}. Magic packets go there unless another one is given below.

data.dangerous_buttons: Show the deep standby and reboot buttons

data_description.dangerous_buttons: Deep standby takes the receiver off the network until a magic packet wakes it, and reboot interrupts whatever it is doing. Both are hidden by default so that neither is one mis-tap away on a shared dashboard. The plugin refuses both while a recording is running, whatever is set here.
data_description.wol_mac: Leave empty to use the address the receiver reports. Set it when the receiver reports a different interface from the one that is plugged in — a box on Wi-Fi does not answer a magic packet sent to its cable port.
data_description.bouquets: Which bouquets the channel list and the media browser offer. Leave empty for every bouquet the receiver publishes.

zap.name: Zap
zap.description: Tunes the receiver to a channel, by service reference or by name. Give exactly one of the two.

sref.name: Service reference
sref.description: The channel's service reference, trailing colon included. This is the identifier that never changes.

name.name: Channel name
name.description: The channel's name as the bouquet spells it. Refused by the receiver when more than one channel in its configured bouquets has that name.

send_key.name: Send key
send_key.description: Injects a remote control key into the receiver, as if somebody had pressed it.

key.name: Key
key.description: The key name, such as `KEY_RED`. `red` works too.

long.name: Long press
long.description: Send it as a held button rather than a tap.

message.name: Show message
message.description: Puts a popup on the television. The receiver cuts the text at 500 characters.

type.name: Type
type.description: Which icon and colour the popup uses.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: How long the popup stays on screen, in seconds.

add_timer.name: Add timer
add_timer.description: Adds a recording timer, either from an EPG event or from a start and end time. Give the event ID, or both times — not both forms.

event_id.name: Event ID
event_id.description: The EPG event to record. Prefer this: the receiver resolves the event itself, so the timer gets the programme's name and the padding the box is set up with.

begin.name: Start
begin.description: When to start recording, for a manual window.

end.name: End
end.description: When to stop recording, for a manual window.

name.name: Name
name.description: What to call the recording, for a manual window.

delete_timer.name: Delete timer
delete_timer.description: Deletes a recording timer. enigma2 identifies a timer by its channel, start and end, so all three are needed.

record.name: Record
record.description: Starts or stops an instant recording of whatever is on.

screenshot.name: Take a screenshot
screenshot.description: Captures what is on the television now and publishes it, which is what refreshes the Screen image entity.

set_ha_mode.name: Set Home Assistant mode
set_ha_mode.description: Switches how the receiver presents itself: through this integration, through MQTT discovery, or not at all. Switching away from integration mode leaves this integration's entities without anything updating them.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Which mode the plugin should run in.

get_epg_grid.name: Get the EPG grid
get_epg_grid.description: Returns what is on, per bouquet, as the receiver last published it. Use it in a template or a script; it is deliberately not an entity attribute, because a grid is tens of kilobytes per bouquet and would be written to the recorder database on every refresh.

bouquet.name: Bouquet
bouquet.description: One bouquet, by name or by slug. Left empty, every published bouquet is returned.

mqtt_not_available.message: The MQTT integration is not available, so the receiver cannot be reached.

command_timeout.message: The receiver did not carry out `{command}`. Check that it is on and that the plugin is running.

zap_needs_one.message: Give either a service reference or a channel name, not both and not neither.

timer_needs_event_or_window.message: A timer needs either an event ID or both a start and an end time.

timer_takes_one_form.message: Give an event ID or a start and end time, not both.

unknown_bouquet.message: The receiver has published no EPG grid for the bouquet {bouquet}.

unknown_channel.message: No channel called {channel} is in the bouquets this receiver offers.

unsupported_media_type.message: A receiver can play a channel, not {media_type}.

wake_on_lan_unavailable.message: The Wake on LAN integration is not set up, so no magic packet can be sent. Add it from Settings, then try again.

no_mac.message: This receiver has not reported a MAC address, so there is nowhere to send a magic packet. Set one in the integration's options.
